subject: EdgeCorp private deployment: evaluation of VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN alternatives
messages:
From: Sam Li <sam.li@edgecorp.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Private deployment connectivity options (EdgeCorp)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. EdgeCorp is moving forward with a private deployment of Redwood in our US production environment and we need your recommendation on which network connectivity pattern to standardize on. High-level constraints:
- Production data must not traverse the public internet in transit (compliance requirement).
- Target steady-state throughput: 6k r/s with bursts to 12k r/s (inference requests).
- Typical session lengths are short but a lot of concurrent sessions; low tail latency is important.
- We want predictable egress cost and minimal ops complexity for our infra team.
- Backup/DR path acceptable to be lower performance as long as encrypted.

Attached is our current topology and a short cost projection. Could you sketch the tradeoffs between VPC peering, PrivateLink (or equivalent provider-managed endpoint), and site-to-site VPN for our setup? We also have a few questions:
1) Is there a clear winner for consistent low tail latency at scale?
2) Which option gives the strongest isolation + simplest auditability for SOC2?
3) Any combinations that make sense (e.g., Primary PrivateLink + VPN fallback)?

Thanks — if it helps we can do a 30‑minute call with infra leaders this week.

Sam Li
Head of Cloud Engineering, EdgeCorp
Attachments: network_comparison_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), mpls_topology_diagram.png (image)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@edgecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options (EdgeCorp)

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints and the attachments. Quick top-level thoughts before we dig into details:
- Short answer: there is no one-size-fits-all; we usually recommend PrivateLink (endpoint services) for production traffic that must avoid the public internet and requires strong logical isolation, combined with a lower-cost site-to-site VPN as a DR/management path. VPC peering is attractive for high-throughput, low-cost connectivity but has operational scaling and cross-account management tradeoffs.

I sketched an initial decision matrix (attached) with the metrics I think matter most: latency, throughput scalability, operational discoverability (how easy to audit), cost predictability, failover options, and required account-level permissions. Can you confirm: EdgeCorp will terminate all customer traffic in a single AWS region for now (us-west-2)? Also, are you using AWS Transit Gateway or a simpler peering model today?

If you prefer, Laura can weigh in on the compliance implications and Marissa can call out typical SRE runbooks for each pattern.

Next steps proposed: 1) confirm region + transit gateway usage, 2) we produce a two-page recommendation (PrivateLink primary + VPN DR or peering where appropriate) with expected costs and SLO implications, 3) review SOW scope (I attached a draft SOW).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options (EdgeCorp)

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 12:03 PM aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear constraints and the attachments. Quick top-level thoughts before we dig into details:
> - Short answer: there is no one-size-fits-all; we usually recommend PrivateLink (endpoint services) for production traffic that must avoid the public internet and requires strong logical isolation, combined with a lower-cost site-to-site VPN as a DR/management path. VPC peering is attractive for high-throughput, low-cost connectivity but has operational scaling and cross-account management tradeoffs.

Couple of compliance-focused comments to add:
- Auditability: PrivateLink gives a clear boundary — traffic appears as interface endpoints in the customer account and we can emit flow logs and endpoint-level access logs tied to their CloudWatch/CloudTrail. That simplifies SOC2 evidence collection.
- Data path control: PrivateLink avoids transitive routing across multiple VPCs by design. If EdgeCorp needs strict per-tenant isolation inside its VPCs, PrivateLink backed by our endpoint service is easier to reason about.
- Throughput/tail-latency: PrivateLink will add a small hop compared to direct peering; at very high sustained r/s (>=10k) cost and throughput considerations push peering or Transit Gateway. For the numbers Sam quoted (6k steady, 12k bursts), we need to test TCP burst behavior — SRE runbooks will include connection pooling and connection reuse to avoid tail latency spikes.

Operational note: If EdgeCorp uses Transit Gateway with attachments for multiple VPCs, PrivateLink still maps cleanly but costs can add up. We should include a sample cost delta and a quick perf test plan in the recommendation.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 22:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Decision and recommended next steps — EdgeCorp private deployment connectivity

Sam / Priya — thanks for the input and patience while we pulled this together. Below is our recommended connectivity pattern and immediate action items.

Recommendation (production):
- Primary: PrivateLink (provider-managed interface endpoints) from EdgeCorp VPC(s) to Redwood endpoint service in us-west-2. Rationale: avoids public internet paths, simplest audit footprint for SOC2, explicit customer-side control over endpoint ENIs.
- Secondary (DR/maintenance): Site-to-site IPsec VPN between EdgeCorp on-prem/MPLS edge and Redwood dedicated edge VPC. Rationale: lower cost for a hot-standby path; acceptable to be slightly higher latency.
- Development / internal-only: VPC peering (or Transit Gateway attachments) where you need very high throughput and low cost inside your own account boundary — e.g., for model training or internal QA clusters.

Tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Latency: measure tail latency in a short perf test. We will provide a runbook to configure connection pooling, keepalive, and aggressive HTTP/2 multiplexing for inference clients.
- Throughput: PrivateLink scales but has ENI and bandwidth constraints per endpoint; we recommend sharding across multiple endpoints and using a lightweight fronting NLB in Redwood's account to distribute connections.
- Cost: PrivateLink introduces per‑GB and per‑hour ENI costs. We included a delta in the attached matrix.
- Auditability & compliance: we will provide a CloudTrail/Flow log mapping and sample evidence package for SOC2 auditors.

Proposed short-term plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Confirm region and whether you want Transit Gateway as part of the design (action: Sam).
2) Run a 2-hour perf test (baseline peering vs PrivateLink) with a small traffic generator we provide (action: Redwood SRE).
3) Draft final SOW and schedule kickoff (action: Redwood PM, see attached draft).

Attachments: sod (SOW draft), perf test checklist, updated network_comparison_matrix.xlsx.

If that aligns, I can schedule the perf test and loop in our infra team for a short implementation runbook.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Solutions & Private Deployments
